lines.text: Is this motion simple harmonic? → check that the acceleration (or resultant force) is proportional to the displacement and directed towards equilibrium, $a = -\omega^2 x$ ({{lesson:3.1}})

Period of a mass on a spring or a pendulum → $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{m}{k}}$ (no $g$) or $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}$ (no mass, small angles only); from timings, divide the time for many oscillations by their number ({{lesson:3.1}})

Displacement or velocity at a given time → find $\phi$ from the starting position and direction, then $x = x_0\sin(\omega t + \phi)$ and $v = \omega x_0\cos(\omega t + \phi)$ in radian mode; at a given position instead, $v = \pm\omega\sqrt{x_0^2 - x^2}$ ({{lesson:3.2}})
Energy of an oscillator → $E_\text{T} = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2x_0^2$ with $x_0$ in metres, $E_\text{p} = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2x^2$, then $E_\text{k} = E_\text{T} - E_\text{p}$ ({{lesson:3.2}})
Wave speed from graphs → read $\lambda$ off a displacement–position graph and $T$ off a displacement–time graph, then $v = f\lambda = \frac{\lambda}{T}$ ({{lesson:3.3}})

Wave crossing a boundary → $f$ stays the same; use $n_1\sin\theta_1 = n_2\sin\theta_2$ with angles from the normal; heading into a smaller $n$ beyond $C$, where $\sin C = \frac{n_2}{n_1}$, gives total internal reflection ({{lesson:3.4}})

Maximum or minimum at a point from two in-phase coherent sources → work out $\frac{\text{path difference}}{\lambda}$: a whole number is constructive, a whole number plus a half is destructive ({{lesson:3.5}})
Wavelength or fringe spacing from a double slit → $s = \frac{\lambda D}{d}$ with every length in metres; take $s$ as the distance across many fringes divided by the number of gaps ({{lesson:3.5}})

Single slit or grating → first single-slit minimum at $\theta = \frac{\lambda}{b}$ in radians; grating maxima at $n\lambda = d\sin\theta$ with $d = \frac{1}{\text{lines per metre}}$; highest order is the whole number below $\frac{d}{\lambda}$ ({{lesson:3.6}})

Harmonic frequency of a string or pipe → sketch it first: fixed or closed end is a node, free or open end an antinode; matching ends $f_n = \frac{nv}{2L}$ for every $n$, unlike ends $f_n = \frac{nv}{4L}$ for odd $n$ only ({{lesson:3.7}})

Speed of a star or galaxy from a spectral line → $v = c\,\frac{\Delta\lambda}{\lambda}$ with $\Delta\lambda$ = observed minus emitted, valid for $v \ll c$; redshift means moving away, blueshift moving towards ({{lesson:3.9}})

Sound from a moving source or heard by a moving observer → $f' = f\,\frac{v}{v \pm u_\text{s}}$ or $f' = f\,\frac{v \pm u_\text{o}}{v}$, speeds relative to the air; choose the sign so that approaching raises $f'$ ({{lesson:3.9}})
